details: Bitcoin dropped below $70,000 to near $65,000, marking its lowest point in two months. This significant decline is largely attributed to a sustained period of Bitcoin ETF outflows, totaling nearly $3 billion over the past 10 days, and MicroStrategy's recent sale of 32 BTC. Investor sentiment has deteriorated, with the Crypto Fear & Greed Index now reflecting "Extreme Fear." Geopolitical tensions and higher-than-expected US inflation are also cited as contributing macroeconomic headwinds.
title: Bitcoin Plunges to Two-Month Low Amid ETF Outflows & MicroStrategy Sale

details: European Central Bank (ECB) policymaker Pierre Wunsch indicated that a potential peace agreement between the US and Iran would likely not deter the ECB from proceeding with an interest rate hike in June. Eurozone inflation rose to 3.2% in May, significantly above the ECB's 2% target, strengthening the case for monetary tightening. The ECB is widely expected to be one of the first G7 central banks to raise rates to combat inflationary pressures.
title: ECB Policymaker Signals June Rate Hike Amid Persistent Inflation

details: The Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) has trimmed its global and US economic growth projections for 2026 and 2027. Concurrently, the organization has increased its global inflation forecast for 2026 from 2.8% to 4%. This revised outlook is primarily driven by anticipated persistent disruptions to Middle East exports and escalating energy prices, painting a picture of a more challenging economic landscape ahead.
title: OECD Lowers Global Growth Forecasts, Warns of Rising Inflation
